title: पक्राउ पुर्जी जारी भएका व्यक्ति धनुषा प्रहरीको नियन्त्रणबाटै छुटे

No ads found for this position जनकपुरधाम । सिरहामा ठगी तथा आपराधिक विश्वासघातको मुद्दामा पक्राउ पुर्जी जारी भएका एक व्यक्तिलाई धनुषा प्रहरीले नियन्त्रणमा लिएर पनि छाडिदिएको आरोप लागेको छ । सिरहाको लहानस्थित इलाका प्रहरी कार्यालयमा गत साउनमा मुद्दा दर्ता भई पक्राउ पुर्जी जारी भएका धनुषाको मिथिला बिहारी नगरपालिका–१ का ५४ वर्षीय कुशेश्वर साहलाई प्रहरीले पक्राउ गरेर पनि छाडिदिएको पीडित पक्षको आरोप छ । शुक्रबार बिहान करिब ११ बजे जनकपुरधाम उपमहानगरपालिका–४ स्थित बंशी चोकको काली होटलनजिकै उनलाई लहानबाट सादा पोसाकमा खटिएका प्रहरीले पक्राउ गरेका थिए । पक्राउपछि हत्कडी लगाएर राखिएका साहलाई पछि मुजेलिया प्रहरीले आफ्नो नियन्त्रणमा लिएको थियो । तर, जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालयसम्म नपुर्‍याई बाटोबाटै छाडिदिएको पीडित पक्षको दाबी छ । साहविरुद्ध सिरहाको मुसहरनियाँस्थित कौशल एग्रो राइस मिलमा धान बिक्री गरेका किसानहरूले ठगी तथा आपराधिक विश्वासघातको जाहेरी दिएका थिए । उक्त मिलका सञ्चालक साहले किसानहरूबाट उधारोमा धान खरिद गरे पनि लामो समयसम्म भुक्तानी नगरेको उनीहरूको आरोप छ । २०८१ सालमा सिरहाको कल्याणपुरका रामनाथ साहले २१ लाख रुपैयाँ, प्रवेश साहले ४ लाख रुपैयाँ तथा बरियारपट्टीका दिनेश साह र अशोक महतोले जनही १० लाख रुपैयाँ बराबरको धान मिललाई बिक्री गरेका थिए । तर, पटकपटक ताकेता गर्दा पनि रकम नपाएपछि उनीहरू प्रहरीको शरणमा पुगेका थिए । पीडितहरू २०८१ पुसमै प्रमाणसहित जाहेरी दिन इलाका प्रहरी कार्यालय लहान पुगेका थिए । तर, प्रहरीले जाहेरी दर्ता गर्न नमानेको उनीहरूको भनाइ छ । त्यसपछि जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय, जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय, मधेश प्रदेश प्रहरी कार्यालय, नेपाल प्रहरी प्रधान कार्यालय र गृह मन्त्रालयसम्म धाउँदा करिब डेढ वर्षपछि मात्रै मुद्दा दर्ता भएको थियो । मुद्दा दर्तापछि सिरहा प्रहरीले साहलाई पक्राउ गर्ने प्रयास गर्दै आएको थियो । उनी जनकपुरधाममा बस्दै आएका कारण पक्राउ गर्न धनुषा प्रहरीको सहयोग मागिएको थियो । तर, पटकपटक प्रयास गर्दा पनि पक्राउ गर्न नसकिएको पीडित पक्षको भनाइ छ । शुक्रबार भने लहानबाट सादा पोसाकमा खटिएका दुई प्रहरी पीडितहरूलाई समेत लिएर जनकपुरधाम पुगेका थिए । पिडारी चोक र मधेश भवनको बीचमा पर्ने काली होटलनजिकै साहको घर छ । लहानबाट आएको टोलीले साहलाई पक्राउ गर्न मुजेलिया प्रहरीसँग सहयोग मागेको थियो । तर, प्रहरी तत्काल घटनास्थलमा पुगेन । वडा प्रहरी चौकी मुजेलियाका इन्चार्ज फणीन्द्र अधिकारीले आफू बिदामा रहेको भन्दै कार्यालयमै सम्पर्क गर्न नेपाल प्रेससँगको कुराकानीमा बताए । यता, चौकीका अर्का सहइन्चार्ज अनिरुद्धप्रसाद गुप्तालाई सम्पर्क गर्दा उनले अर्का प्रहरी नायब निरीक्षक (सई) सँग कुरा गर्न भन्दै फोन काटे । उनले अर्का सई वीरेन्द्र साहसँग कुरा गर्न भने पनि उनको सम्पर्क नम्बर भने उपलब्ध गराएनन् । लहानबाट आएको प्रहरी टोलीले साहलाई घरअगाडि नै हत्कडी लगाएर नियन्त्रणमा लिएको थियो । तर, मुजेलिया प्रहरी कार्यालय घटनास्थलबाट करिब एक किलोमिटर मात्रै टाढा भए पनि प्रहरी पुग्न ४० देखि ४५ मिनेट लागेको पीडित रामनाथ साहका छोरा रवीन्द्र साहले बताए । ‘कुशेश्वरलाई प्रहरीले गाडीमा बसाएपछि हामी ढुक्क भयौँ । स्वास्थ्य परीक्षण गरेर जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय ल्याउँछन् भन्ने ठानेर हामी त्यहाँ गयौँ,’ रवीन्द्रले भने, ‘तर, धेरै बेरसम्म नआएपछि मुजेलिया प्रहरीमा पुग्यौँ । त्यहाँ माथिबाट फोन आएपछि छाडिदियौँ भन्ने जवाफ दिइयो ।’ उनका अनुसार मुजेलिया प्रहरीले साहलाई आफ्नो गाडीमा राखेर लगेपछि लहानबाट आएका प्रहरीलाई घटनास्थलमै छाडेको थियो । त्यसपछि लहानबाट आएका प्रहरी र पीडितहरू जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय धनुषा पुगेका थिए । तर, साहलाई त्यहाँ नल्याइएपछि उनीहरू पुनः मुजेलिया प्रहरी कार्यालय पुगेका थिए । त्यहाँ साहलाई नभेटेपछि सोधपुछ गर्दा ‘माथिबाट फोन आएपछि छाडिदिएको’ जवाफ प्रहरीले दिएको रवीन्द्रको दाबी छ । प्रहरीले साहलाई कार्यालयसम्म नल्याई बाटोबाटै घर पुर्‍याइदिएको पीडित पक्षको आरोप छ । रवीन्द्रका अनुसार उनीहरू साहको घर पुग्दा स्थानीयले केही समयअघि मात्रै प्रहरीले उनलाई घर पुर्‍याइदिएको बताएका थिए । उक्त घटनाको दृश्य घरनजिकैको सीसीटीभीमा समेत कैद भएको उनको दाबी छ । पीडितहरूले साहलाई पक्राउ गरेर प्रहरीको जिम्मा लगाएको दृश्यको भिडियो र तस्बिरसमेत खिचेका छन् । यता, जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय धनुषाका डीएसपी एवं प्रवक्ता ओमप्रकाश खनालले भने यस विषयमा आफूलाई जानकारी नभएको बताए । नेपाल प्रेससँग प्रतिक्रिया दिँदै उनले घटनाबारे बुझ्न बाँकी रहेको र त्यसपछि मात्रै थप प्रतिक्रिया दिन सक्ने बताए । Janakpurdham. There are allegations that Dhanusha police have taken into custody a person who was issued an arrest warrant in Siraha for fraud and criminal breach of trust but then released him. The victim's side alleges that the police arrested and released 54-year-old Kusheshwor Sah, of Mithila Bihari Municipality-1, Dhanusha, after a case was registered at the Area Police Office in Lahan, Siraha, and an arrest warrant was issued in July. He was arrested by plainclothes police deployed from Lahan near the Kali Hotel in Banshi Chowk, Janakpurdham Sub-metropolitan City-4, on Friday morning at around 11 am. Sah, who was handcuffed after his arrest, was later taken into custody by the Muzeliya police. However, the victim claims that he was released on the road without being taken to the District Police Office. Farmers who sold rice to Kaushal Agro Rice Mill in Musaharniya, Siraha, had filed a complaint of fraud and criminal breach of trust against Sah. They allege that Sah, the mill's operator, had purchased rice from the farmers on credit but had not paid for a long time. In 2081 BS, Ramnath Sah of Kalyanpur, Siraha, sold rice worth Rs. 2.1 million, Pravesh Sah of Rs. 4 million, and Dinesh Sah and Ashok Mahato of Bariyarpatti each sold rice worth Rs. 1 million to a rice mill. However, after not receiving the money despite repeated requests, they went to the police. The victims had reached the Area Police Office, Lahan, to file a complaint with evidence in December 2002. However, they say that the police refused to register the complaint. After that, they went to the District Police Office, District Administration Office, Madhesh Province Police Office, Nepal Police Headquarters, and the Ministry of Home Affairs, but the case was registered only after about a year and a half. After the case was registered, Siraha police had been trying to arrest Sah. Since he was living in Janakpurdham, Dhanusha police had been asked to help arrest him. However, the victim's side says that despite repeated attempts, they could not arrest him. On Friday, two plainclothes police officers from Lahan reached Janakpurdham along with the victims. Sah's house is near Kali Hotel, which is located between Pidari Chowk and Madhesh Bhawan. The team from Lahan had sought help from Mujelia police to arrest Sah. However, the police did not immediately reach the spot. In an interview with Nepal Press, Phanindra Adhikari, in-charge of Mujelia Ward Police Station, said he was on leave and asked to contact the office. Meanwhile, when contacted, Aniruddha Prasad Gupta, another deputy in-charge of the post, said he would like to speak to another Deputy Inspector of Police (DIP), but he hung up. He also said he would like to speak to another DIP, Birendra Sah, but did not provide his contact number. A police team from Lahan had handcuffed Sah and taken him into custody in front of his house. However, even though the Mujelia Police Office is only about a kilometer away from the incident site, it took 40 to 45 minutes for the police to reach there, said Rabindra Sah, son of victim Ramnath Sah. "We felt relieved after the police put Kusheshwar in the vehicle. We went there thinking that he would take us to the District Police Office after a health check," said Rabindra. "However, after he did not come for a long time, we reached Mujelia Police Station. We were told that we had been released after receiving a call from above." According to him, the Mujelia police left the police from Lahan at the scene after taking Sah in their vehicle. After that, the police from Lahan and the victims reached the District Police Office, Dhanusha. However, when Sah was not brought there, they returned to the Mujelia Police Office. Rabindra claims that when questioned after not finding Sah there, the police replied that he left after receiving a call from above. The victim's side alleges that the police took Sah home on the road instead of taking him to the office. According to Rabindra, when they reached Sah's house, locals said that the police had taken him home only a short while ago. He claims that the incident was also captured on CCTV near the house. The victims have also taken videos and photographs of the scene where Sah was arrested and handed over to the police. Meanwhile, DSP and spokesperson of the District Police Office, Dhanusha, Om Prakash Khanal, said that he was not aware of this matter. Responding to Nepal Press, he said that the incident is yet to be understood and only then can he give further feedback.

There are allegations that Dhanusha police have taken into custody a person who was issued an arrest warrant in Siraha for fraud and criminal breach of trust but then released him. The victim's side alleges that the police arrested and released 54-year-old Kusheshwor Sah, of Mithila Bihari Municipality-1, Dhanusha, after a case was registered at the Area Police Office in Lahan, Siraha, and an arrest warrant was issued in July. He was arrested by plainclothes police deployed from Lahan near the Kali Hotel in Banshi Chowk, Janakpurdham Sub-metropolitan City-4, on Friday morning at around 11 am. Sah, who was handcuffed after his arrest, was later taken into custody by the Muzeliya police. However, the victim claims that he was released on the road without being taken to the District Police Office. Farmers who sold rice to Kaushal Agro Rice Mill in Musaharniya, Siraha, had filed a complaint of fraud and criminal breach of trust against Sah. They allege that Sah, the mill's operator, had purchased rice from the farmers on credit but had not paid for a long time. In 2081 BS, Ramnath Sah of Kalyanpur, Siraha, sold rice worth Rs. 2.1 million, Pravesh Sah of Rs. 4 million, and Dinesh Sah and Ashok Mahato of Bariyarpatti each sold rice worth Rs. 1 million to a rice mill. However, after not receiving the money despite repeated requests, they went to the police. The victims had reached the Area Police Office, Lahan, to file a complaint with evidence in December 2002. However, they say that the police refused to register the complaint. After that, they went to the District Police Office, District Administration Office, Madhesh Province Police Office, Nepal Police Headquarters, and the Ministry of Home Affairs, but the case was registered only after about a year and a half. After the case was registered, Siraha police had been trying to arrest Sah. Since he was living in Janakpurdham, Dhanusha police had been asked to help arrest him. However, the victim's side says that despite repeated attempts, they could not arrest him. On Friday, two plainclothes police officers from Lahan reached Janakpurdham along with the victims. Sah's house is near Kali Hotel, which is located between Pidari Chowk and Madhesh Bhawan. The team from Lahan had sought help from Mujelia police to arrest Sah. However, the police did not immediately reach the spot. Meanwhile, when contacted, Aniruddha Prasad Gupta, another deputy in-charge of the post, said he would like to speak to another Deputy Inspector of Police (DIP), but he hung up. He also said he would like to speak to another DIP, Birendra Sah, but did not provide his contact number. A police team from Lahan had handcuffed Sah and taken him into custody in front of his house. However, even though the Mujelia Police Office is only about a kilometer away from the incident site, it took 40 to 45 minutes for the police to reach there, said Rabindra Sah, son of victim Ramnath Sah. "We felt relieved after the police put Kusheshwar in the vehicle. We went there thinking that he would take us to the District Police Office after a health check," said Rabindra. "However, after he did not come for a long time, we reached Mujelia Police Station. We were told that we had been released after receiving a call from above." According to him, the Mujelia police left the police from Lahan at the scene after taking Sah in their vehicle. After that, the police from Lahan and the victims reached the District Police Office, Dhanusha. However, when Sah was not brought there, they returned to the Mujelia Police Office. Rabindra claims that when questioned after not finding Sah there, the police replied that he left after receiving a call from above. The victim's side alleges that the police took Sah home on the road instead of taking him to the office. Meanwhile, DSP and spokesperson of the District Police Office, Dhanusha, Om Prakash Khanal, said that he was not aware of this matter. Responding to Nepal Press, he said that the incident is yet to be understood and only then can he give further feedback.

There are allegations that Dhanusha police have taken into custody a person who was issued an arrest warrant in Siraha for fraud and criminal breach of trust but then released him. The victim's side alleges that the police arrested and released 54-year-old Kusheshwor Sah, of Mithila Bihari Municipality-1, Dhanusha, after a case was registered at the Area Police Office in Lahan, Siraha, and an arrest warrant was issued in July. He was arrested by plainclothes police deployed from Lahan near the Kali Hotel in Banshi Chowk, Janakpurdham Sub-metropolitan City-4, on Friday morning at around 11 am. Sah, who was handcuffed after his arrest, was later taken into custody by the Muzeliya police. However, the victim claims that he was released on the road without being taken to the District Police Office. Farmers who sold rice to Kaushal Agro Rice Mill in Musaharniya, Siraha, had filed a complaint of fraud and criminal breach of trust against Sah. They allege that Sah, the mill's operator, had purchased rice from the farmers on credit but had not paid for a long time. In 2081 BS, Ramnath Sah of Kalyanpur, Siraha, sold rice worth Rs. 2.1 million, Pravesh Sah of Rs. 4 million, and Dinesh Sah and Ashok Mahato of Bariyarpatti each sold rice worth Rs. 1 million to a rice mill. However, after not receiving the money despite repeated requests, they went to the police. The victims had reached the Area Police Office, Lahan, to file a complaint with evidence in December 2002. However, they say that the police refused to register the complaint. After that, they went to the District Police Office, District Administration Office, Madhesh Province Police Office, Nepal Police Headquarters, and the Ministry of Home Affairs, but the case was registered only after about a year and a half. After the case was registered, Siraha police had been trying to arrest Sah. Since he was living in Janakpurdham, Dhanusha police had been asked to help arrest him. However, the victim's side says that despite repeated attempts, they could not arrest him. On Friday, two plainclothes police officers from Lahan reached Janakpurdham along with the victims. Sah's house is near Kali Hotel, which is located between Pidari Chowk and Madhesh Bhawan. The team from Lahan had sought help from Mujelia police to arrest Sah. However, the police did not immediately reach the spot. In an interview with Nepal Press, Phanindra Adhikari, in-charge of Mujelia Ward Police Station, said he was on leave and asked to contact the office. Meanwhile, when contacted, Aniruddha Prasad Gupta, another deputy in-charge of the post, said he would like to speak to another Deputy Inspector of Police (DIP), but he hung up. He also said he would like to speak to another DIP, Birendra Sah, but did not provide his contact number. A police team from Lahan had handcuffed Sah and taken him into custody in front of his house. However, even though the Mujelia Police Office is only about a kilometer away from the incident site, it took 40 to 45 minutes for the police to reach there, said Rabindra Sah, son of victim Ramnath Sah. "We felt relieved after the police put Kusheshwar in the vehicle. We went there thinking that he would take us to the District Police Office after a health check," said Rabindra. "However, after he did not come for a long time, we reached Mujelia Police Station. We were told that we had been released after receiving a call from above." According to him, the Mujelia police left the police from Lahan at the scene after taking Sah in their vehicle. After that, the police from Lahan and the victims reached the District Police Office, Dhanusha. However, when Sah was not brought there, they returned to the Mujelia Police Office. Rabindra claims that when questioned after not finding Sah there, the police replied that he left after receiving a call from above. The victim's side alleges that the police took Sah home on the road instead of taking him to the office. According to Rabindra, when they reached Sah's house, locals said that the police had taken him home only a short while ago. He claims that the incident was also captured on CCTV near the house. The victims have also taken videos and photographs of the scene where Sah was arrested and handed over to the police. Meanwhile, DSP and spokesperson of the District Police Office, Dhanusha, Om Prakash Khanal, said that he was not aware of this matter. Responding to Nepal Press, he said that the incident is yet to be understood and only then can he give further feedback.

There are allegations that Dhanusha police have taken into custody a person who was issued an arrest warrant in Siraha for fraud and criminal breach of trust but then released him. The victim's side alleges that the police arrested and released 54-year-old Kusheshwor Sah, of Mithila Bihari Municipality-1, Dhanusha, after a case was registered at the Area Police Office in Lahan, Siraha, and an arrest warrant was issued in July. He was arrested by plainclothes police deployed from Lahan near the Kali Hotel in Banshi Chowk, Janakpurdham Sub-metropolitan City-4, on Friday morning at around 11 am. Sah, who was handcuffed after his arrest, was later taken into custody by the Muzeliya police. However, the victim claims that he was released on the road without being taken to the District Police Office. Farmers who sold rice to Kaushal Agro Rice Mill in Musaharniya, Siraha, had filed a complaint of fraud and criminal breach of trust against Sah. पीडितहरू २०८१ पुसमै प्रमाणसहित जाहेरी दिन इलाका प्रहरी कार्यालय लहान पुगेका थिए । तर, प्रहरीले जाहेरी दर्ता गर्न नमानेको उनीहरूको भनाइ छ । त्यसपछि जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय, जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय, मधेश प्रदेश प्रहरी कार्यालय, नेपाल प्रहरी प्रधान कार्यालय र गृह मन्त्रालयसम्म धाउँदा करिब डेढ वर्षपछि मात्रै मुद्दा दर्ता भएको थियो ।

मुद्दा दर्तापछि सिरहा प्रहरीले साहलाई पक्राउ गर्ने प्रयास गर्दै आएको थियो । उनी जनकपुरधाममा बस्दै आएका कारण पक्राउ गर्न धनुषा प्रहरीको सहयोग मागिएको थियो । तर, पटकपटक प्रयास गर्दा पनि पक्राउ गर्न नसकिएको पीडित पक्षको भनाइ छ ।

शुक्रबार भने लहानबाट सादा पोसाकमा खटिएका दुई प्रहरी पीडितहरूलाई समेत लिएर जनकपुरधाम पुगेका थिए । पिडारी चोक र मधेश भवनको बीचमा पर्ने काली होटलनजिकै साहको घर छ । लहानबाट आएको टोलीले साहलाई पक्राउ गर्न मुजेलिया प्रहरीसँग सहयोग मागेको थियो । तर, प्रहरी तत्काल घटनास्थलमा पुगेन ।

वडा प्रहरी चौकी मुजेलियाका इन्चार्ज फणीन्द्र अधिकारीले आफू बिदामा रहेको भन्दै कार्यालयमै सम्पर्क गर्न नेपाल प्रेससँगको कुराकानीमा बताए ।

यता, चौकीका अर्का सहइन्चार्ज अनिरुद्धप्रसाद गुप्तालाई सम्पर्क गर्दा उनले अर्का प्रहरी नायब निरीक्षक (सई) सँग कुरा गर्न भन्दै फोन काटे । उनले अर्का सई वीरेन्द्र साहसँग कुरा गर्न भने पनि उनको सम्पर्क नम्बर भने उपलब्ध गराएनन् ।

लहानबाट आएको प्रहरी टोलीले साहलाई घरअगाडि नै हत्कडी लगाएर नियन्त्रणमा लिएको थियो । तर, मुजेलिया प्रहरी कार्यालय घटनास्थलबाट करिब एक किलोमिटर मात्रै टाढा भए पनि प्रहरी पुग्न ४० देखि ४५ मिनेट लागेको पीडित रामनाथ साहका छोरा रवीन्द्र साहले बताए ।

‘कुशेश्वरलाई प्रहरीले गाडीमा बसाएपछि हामी ढुक्क भयौँ । स्वास्थ्य परीक्षण गरेर जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय ल्याउँछन् भन्ने ठानेर हामी त्यहाँ गयौँ,’ रवीन्द्रले भने, ‘तर, धेरै बेरसम्म नआएपछि मुजेलिया प्रहरीमा पुग्यौँ । त्यहाँ माथिबाट फोन आएपछि छाडिदियौँ भन्ने जवाफ दिइयो ।’

उनका अनुसार मुजेलिया प्रहरीले साहलाई आफ्नो गाडीमा राखेर लगेपछि लहानबाट आएका प्रहरीलाई घटनास्थलमै छाडेको थियो । त्यसपछि लहानबाट आएका प्रहरी र पीडितहरू जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय धनुषा पुगेका थिए । तर, साहलाई त्यहाँ नल्याइएपछि उनीहरू पुनः मुजेलिया प्रहरी कार्यालय पुगेका थिए ।

त्यहाँ साहलाई नभेटेपछि सोधपुछ गर्दा ‘माथिबाट फोन आएपछि छाडिदिएको’ जवाफ प्रहरीले दिएको रवीन्द्रको दाबी छ ।

प्रहरीले साहलाई कार्यालयसम्म नल्याई बाटोबाटै घर पुर्‍याइदिएको पीडित पक्षको आरोप छ । रवीन्द्रका अनुसार उनीहरू साहको घर पुग्दा स्थानीयले केही समयअघि मात्रै प्रहरीले उनलाई घर पुर्‍याइदिएको बताएका थिए । उक्त घटनाको दृश्य घरनजिकैको सीसीटीभीमा समेत कैद भएको उनको दाबी छ ।

पीडितहरूले साहलाई पक्राउ गरेर प्रहरीको जिम्मा लगाएको दृश्यको भिडियो र तस्बिरसमेत खिचेका छन् ।

यता, जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय धनुषाका डीएसपी एवं प्रवक्ता ओमप्रकाश खनालले भने यस विषयमा आफूलाई जानकारी नभएको बताए । नेपाल प्रेससँग प्रतिक्रिया दिँदै उनले घटनाबारे बुझ्न बाँकी रहेको र त्यसपछि मात्रै थप प्रतिक्रिया दिन सक्ने बताए ।

Janakpurdham. There are allegations that Dhanusha police have taken into custody a person who was issued an arrest warrant in Siraha for fraud and criminal breach of trust but then released him. The victim's side alleges that the police arrested and released 54-year-old Kusheshwor Sah, of Mithila Bihari Municipality-1, Dhanusha, after a case was registered at the Area Police Office in Lahan, Siraha, and an arrest warrant was issued in July. He was arrested by plainclothes police deployed from Lahan near the Kali Hotel in Banshi Chowk, Janakpurdham Sub-metropolitan City-4, on Friday morning at around 11 am. Sah, who was handcuffed after his arrest, was later taken into custody by the Muzeliya police. However, the victim claims that he was released on the road without being taken to the District Police Office. Farmers who sold rice to Kaushal Agro Rice Mill in Musaharniya, Siraha, had filed a complaint of fraud and criminal breach of trust against Sah. They allege that Sah, the mill's operator, had purchased rice from the farmers on credit but had not paid for a long time. In 2081 BS, Ramnath Sah of Kalyanpur, Siraha, sold rice worth Rs. 2.1 million, Pravesh Sah of Rs. 4 million, and Dinesh Sah and Ashok Mahato of Bariyarpatti each sold rice worth Rs. 1 million to a rice mill. However, after not receiving the money despite repeated requests, they went to the police. The victims had reached the Area Police Office, Lahan, to file a complaint with evidence in December 2002. However, they say that the police refused to register the complaint. After that, they went to the District Police Office, District Administration Office, Madhesh Province Police Office, Nepal Police Headquarters, and the Ministry of Home Affairs, but the case was registered only after about a year and a half. After the case was registered, Siraha police had been trying to arrest Sah. Since he was living in Janakpurdham, Dhanusha police had been asked to help arrest him. However, the victim's side says that despite repeated attempts, they could not arrest him. On Friday, two plainclothes police officers from Lahan reached Janakpurdham along with the victims. Sah's house is near Kali Hotel, which is located between Pidari Chowk and Madhesh Bhawan. The team from Lahan had sought help from Mujelia police to arrest Sah. However, the police did not immediately reach the spot. In an interview with Nepal Press, Phanindra Adhikari, in-charge of Mujelia Ward Police Station, said he was on leave and asked to contact the office. Meanwhile, when contacted, Aniruddha Prasad Gupta, another deputy in-charge of the post, said he would like to speak to another Deputy Inspector of Police (DIP), but he hung up. He also said he would like to speak to another DIP, Birendra Sah, but did not provide his contact number. A police team from Lahan had handcuffed Sah and taken him into custody in front of his house. However, even though the Mujelia Police Office is only about a kilometer away from the incident site, it took 40 to 45 minutes for the police to reach there, said Rabindra Sah, son of victim Ramnath Sah. "We felt relieved after the police put Kusheshwar in the vehicle. We went there thinking that he would take us to the District Police Office after a health check," said Rabindra. "However, after he did not come for a long time, we reached Mujelia Police Station. We were told that we had been released after receiving a call from above." According to him, the Mujelia police left the police from Lahan at the scene after taking Sah in their vehicle. After that, the police from Lahan and the victims reached the District Police Office, Dhanusha. However, when Sah was not brought there, they returned to the Mujelia Police Office. Rabindra claims that when questioned after not finding Sah there, the police replied that he left after receiving a call from above. The victim's side alleges that the police took Sah home on the road instead of taking him to the office. According to Rabindra, when they reached Sah's house, locals said that the police had taken him home only a short while ago. He claims that the incident was also captured on CCTV near the house. The victims have also taken videos and photographs of the scene where Sah was arrested and handed over to the police. Meanwhile, DSP and spokesperson of the District Police Office, Dhanusha, Om Prakash Khanal, said that he was not aware of this matter. Responding to Nepal Press, he said that the incident is yet to be understood and only then can he give further feedback.
